what_it_does: Neural networks are built from mathematical building blocks called operators (like the operation that multiplies two matrices, or the operation that picks the strongest signal among many). Today, humans design these operators by hand and then use software tools to optimize how they run on hardware. Syno asks a more ambitious question: can a computer automatically invent brand-new operators that humans haven't tried? It defines a small set of elementary actions that can be combined to build operators, and enforces rules that guarantee any invented operator will actually be trainable (mathematically stable). A randomized search — similar to how a chess engine explores possible moves — hunts through the space of combinations and evaluates promising candidates by compiling and running them on real hardware.
